_comment: Deny-list seccomp profile for ContainerSandbox action containers. Default action is ALLOW (the container only ever runs a fixed, trusted Python entrypoint against a stock base image, not arbitrary code) with an explicit ERRNO block on syscall groups a guarded-action effect has no legitimate reason to call: namespace/mount manipulation, kernel module loading, raw process tracing/injection, direct kernel memory or module access, and system-control operations (reboot, swap, time). Combined with --cap-drop=ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges, a non-root user, and a read-only root filesystem, most of these are already unreachable without CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_MODULE/etc.; blocking the syscalls too is defence in depth against a kernel bug that makes a 'dropped' capability check bypassable. A stricter default-deny allowlist (Docker's own default profile is one) is the natural next hardening step for a production deployment -- see docs/sandbox.md.
